title: A Space website carries its Contact form as a themed message section and a Contact page with the owner's profile, every message landing in the CRM

source.ref: Owner ask 2026-10-07: 'Make sure I have a contact form on the main page all tied in, as well as a contact page with more info about me. Do a profile over there', and 'The contact functions need to be fully integrated with the CRM. we built a block for this.' Follows LIVE-830.

detail: FILED AND CLOSED 2026-10-07. THE CONSEQUENCE: the house website theme (LIVE-830) had no place for the Contact form block, so a form placed on Home fell into an unthemed band, and a website had no Contact page at all (contact is a reserved slug, so the owner could not make one). The Space Contact tab showed the form and hours but nothing about the person. THE FIX: the planner gives `contactForm` its own message section, drawn with the same CRM-wired form (submitContactForm writes the lead and emails the owner); the thank-you offers the Space's header button. Once the form is on Home, the website serves /contact: a profile from the About block (its heading and text, the Zigzag photo, the facts), the form, and the closing band with the contact details; the header gains a Contact link and the sitemap lists it. The Space Contact tab gains the same profile. Every word is the Space's own field. The `*accent*` marks drop on the Space page (withoutAccentMarks), since Daniel's live headings now carry them. The website hero gets its own words: Website headline and Website intro on the Profile & Settings Website card (preferences.siteHero) lead the website hero, falling back to the Hero settings, so the Space page header keeps the Space name while the website leads with a marketing line.

verify.note: Fails on main (no message section, no website Contact page); passes once this lands.
